clue.text: One comes together for sponsors

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'One comes together for sponsors', gives no wordplay for ANGELS: 'sponsors' defines it but 'One comes together' yields no letters; likely garbled in OCR.

clue.text: Are two of 24 normally found in pairs?

indicators.note: the cross-reference points to the answer at 24, which spells out the anagram device, so these letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether a couple of items from some puzzle always come as a matching pair.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' is the cross-reference to the light ANAGRAM, used as the anagram signal: rearrange ARE TWO OF.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoes and boots are worn as a matched left and right, so footwear normally comes in pairs.

clue.text: This particular research group is sure to waste reserves on electric current

indicators.note: to waste something is to lose it, so these letters are thrown away from the longer word

parts.note: sure means certain
TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer military reserve
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A remark about a lab group that is bound to squander backup funds on electricity bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets TA beside I, and 'to waste' removes that TAI run from CERTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: CERN is the European laboratory for particle physics near Geneva, a famous research organisation.

clue.text: Cultural all-rounder managed to capture 24 of maniacs seen

indicators.note: to capture is to hold within, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: managed means ran, as in ran a business

indicators.note: the cross-reference names the light that spells out the anagram device, so an anagram of the following words is meant

explanation.surface: A versatile cultured person managed to snare a rearrangement of some lunatics who were spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: '24 of' refers to the light ANAGRAM: rearranging MANIACS SEEN gives ENAISSANCEM, which 'to capture' puts inside RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Renaissance man is a polymath with wide learning and accomplishment across many arts and sciences.

clue.text: Person shouting about Florida's campanula

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the shouter goes around the state's abbreviation

parts.note: someone who bellows is a bellower
FL is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Florida

explanation.surface: A loud person from Florida apparently owns a particular garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Campanula is the botanical genus whose bell-shaped blooms are commonly called by this name.

clue.text: He designed lights for rent is sorted

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'He designed lights for rent is sorted', defines the lighthouse engineer but 'for rent is sorted' cannot give the letters of ROBERT STEVENSON; likely garbled in OCR.
annotationWithheld.clue: He designed lights for rent is sorted

clue.text: A head for the movies

parts.note: a headland (a head) whose name is also the title of two films, the 1962 thriller and its 1991 remake

explanation.surface: Someone said to have a natural talent for cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: This North Carolina headland lent its name to two thriller films, so it is a promontory famous on screen.

clue.text: Cipher number!

parts.note: a cipher is a nobody, a person of no account; read as a figure, the cipher zero is the number standing for not even one

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a figure used in a secret code.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is a nonentity, a person who counts for nothing, and zero is the count of nobody.

clue.text: English distance runner from South Africa's given name for writer

parts.note: a mile is a measure of distance

parts.words: runner from South Africa's given name
parts.note: Zola Budd was a barefoot South African middle-distance runner of the 1980s, and Zola is her first name

explanation.surface: Biographical trivia about an English athlete, a South African runner and a writer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist of the Rougon-Macquart cycle and author of 'J'accuse' was a celebrated author.

clue.text: A natural reaction to a bug crawling around menu on premises

definitions.text: A natural reaction to a bug

indicators.note: letters crawling around move about out of order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An insect creeping over a restaurant's menu prompts a natural reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'bug' is an insect; the definition's 'bug' is an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's defence against infection by a germ is its natural immunological reaction.

clue.text: First class fly half returns to take on country

indicators.note: to take in is to hold inside, so one piece is placed within the other
returns means the combined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here with I for 1

indicators.note: half signals that only the first half of the insect's name is used

parts.note: the tsetse is an African fly

explanation.surface: A rugby fly-half of the first rank comes back to take on a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: AI plus TSE (half of TSETSE) reversed gives ESTIA, and 'to take' puts ON inside it. 'Fly half' looks like the rugby position.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic nation on the Gulf of Finland.

clue.text: French writer heard Miss Malone in Dublin's fair city, for example?

indicators.note: heard signals that the letters come from how the phrase is spoken

parts.words: Miss Malone in Dublin's fair city, for example
parts.note: Molly Malone is the girl of the Irish song beginning 'In Dublin's fair city', so the song is a Molly air

explanation.surface: A French author hearing the famous Dublin ballad about a fishmonger girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The song 'Molly Malone' opens 'In Dublin's fair city'; 'Molly air' (a Molly song) said aloud gives the playwright's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventeenth-century playwright of Tartuffe is a classic French dramatist.

clue.text: See 6Down
Centre of Bexhill on Sea in the end needs speed to thrill

indicators.note: the centre of a word is all of it but its first and last letters
in the end points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: rate means speed

explanation.surface: A visit to the middle of the English seaside town of Bexhill-on-Sea needs pace to excite.
explanation.walkthrough: Bexhill-on-Sea is a resort on England's south coast; its name is split here into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhilarate is to make someone lively and elated, i.e. to excite.

clue.text: Drunk on less than two pints

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone getting drunk on under two pints of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is about 1.76 imperial pints, a metric measure just short of two.

clue.text: What? Mr Garfunkel's entering ground!

indicators.note: entering means going inside the other word

parts.note: eh is a word for what, asking for a repeat
Art Garfunkel is the singer of Simon and Garfunkel

explanation.surface: Surprise that the singer Mr Garfunkel is walking onto a sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground is soil or land underfoot, the same as earth.

clue.text: English politician has island accent

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: An English politician with an island constituency speaks with a regional accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Accent can mean stress or prominence given to something, the same as emphasis.

clue.text: flies through it

parts.note: the medium through which birds, insects and aircraft fly

explanation.surface: A short note about what something travels through.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds and planes move in the atmosphere, the gas around the Earth.

clue.text: You can't get things neat with it

definitions.text: You can't get things neat with it

parts.words: You can't get things neat with it
parts.note: a drink served neat is undiluted, so adding this liquid stops it being neat

explanation.surface: A complaint about a cleaning product that never leaves things tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat spirits are taken undiluted, with nothing like a splash from the tap added.

clue.text: Bird (a booby) and another one losing its tail crossing motorway

parts.note: a tit is slang for a fool, a booby
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

indicators.note: losing its tail means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an ousel (ouzel) is another bird, the blackbird or ring ouzel
the tail of the bird's name is its final letter, which is dropped

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's note about a foolish bird and a tailless companion crossing a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: '(a booby)' looks like a gloss on the bird, but it gives TIT; 'losing its tail' drops the L of OUSEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Titmouse is an older name for the tit, a small songbird.

clue.text: Ring Around the Roses, just a bit?

definitions.text: Ring Around the Roses, just a bit?

parts.words: Ring Around the Roses, just a bit?
parts.note: the coloured leaves arranged in a ring around a rose's centre, each just a small part of the flower

explanation.surface: A question about the children's nursery game Ring a Ring o' Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the ring of coloured leaves forming a flower's corolla is one small part of a bloom.

clue.text: Gratitude for one getting to play R Langdon

definitions.meaning: gratitude is appreciation expressed to someone

definitions.text: one getting to play R Langdon
definitions.meaning: Tom Hanks, written ..., played the professor Robert Langdon in The Da Vinci Code films

explanation.surface: A note of appreciation for the actor cast as Robert Langdon.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratitude is expressed as appreciation, and the actor T. Hanks played the symbologist Robert Langdon.

clue.text: Players judged to be no longer knackered

parts.note: the players in a production are its cast
rated means judged or assessed

explanation.surface: Actors assessed as no longer being worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knackered' looks like exhausted; here it is read as having knackers, British slang for testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Castration removes the testicles, so a castrated animal no longer has its family jewels.

clue.text: Protests about inn finally serving up spirits that are bad

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the protests go around the letter

parts.note: demos are protest marches

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Protests about a pub that finally serves up bad spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Demons are evil supernatural beings, malevolent spirits.

clue.text: Puzzle involving a horse and sheep

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A puzzle featuring a horse and a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A word rearranged into another is a kind of word puzzle.

clue.text: Leaders of oil firm find first oil rig manager's not operating well …

indicators.note: leaders are the front runners, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: An oil company's bosses discover that its first rig manager isn't working properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off form means playing or working below one's usual standard.

clue.text: Fellow with anger to let off

parts.note: ire means anger

explanation.surface: A man in a temper being told off or excused.
explanation.definitionFit: To let off a gun or firework is to discharge it.

clue.text: … and Texaco initially sinks 24 wells storing black liquid here maybe

definitions.text: wells storing black liquid here maybe

indicators.note: the cross-reference names the light that spells out the anagram device, so the preceding letters are rearranged
initially points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An oil company sinks wells and stores crude oil there.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' is the cross-reference to ANAGRAM, the anagram signal: rearrange AND, T and SINKS. The wells are inkwells, not oil wells.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkstand is a desk stand holding inkwells, pots for ink.

clue.text: Touching Evil is sappy stuff

parts.note: re means touching on or concerning
sin is evil or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A heartfelt take on wickedness is mawkish.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the sticky substance exuded as sap by trees such as pines.
